questions.question_text: Which of these ways of writing $840\,000$ is in scientific notation?

options.why: Equal in value, but the coefficient $84$ is not less than $10$, so this is not scientific notation.
Equal in value, but the coefficient $0.84$ is less than $1$, so this is not scientific notation.
Equal in value, but the coefficient $840$ is far outside $1 \le a < 10$, so this is not scientific notation.

questions.solution_text:
In scientific notation the coefficient must satisfy $1 \le a < 10$.
$840\,000 = 8.4 \times 10^{5}$

questions.question_text: What is $93\,000\,000$ written in scientific notation?

options.why: Counted the six zeros instead of the seven places the decimal point moves.
Left the coefficient as $93$ instead of moving the decimal point to sit after the first digit.
Used a negative power, but $93\,000\,000$ is a large number so the power must be positive.

questions.solution_text:
The decimal point moves $7$ places to sit after the $9$.
$93\,000\,000$
$=9.3 \times 10^{7}$

questions.question_text: What is $0.000\,46$ written in scientific notation?

options.why: Counted only the three zeros after the decimal point instead of the four places the decimal point moves.
Used a positive power, but $0.000\,46$ is a small number so the power must be negative.
Moved the decimal point one place too far, going past the first non-zero digit.

questions.solution_text:
The decimal point moves $4$ places to sit after the $4$; a small number takes a negative power.
$0.000\,46$
$=4.6 \times 10^{-4}$

options.why: Appended four zeros after $506$ instead of moving the decimal point four places from after the $5$.
Moved the decimal point only three places instead of four.
Moved the decimal point to the left as if the power were negative.

questions.solution_text:
The power $4$ is positive, so move the decimal point $4$ places to the right.
$5.06 \times 10^{4}$
$=50\,600$

options.why: Placed three zeros before the digits instead of moving the decimal point three places.
Moved the decimal point only two places instead of three.
Ignored the negative sign and moved the decimal point to the right instead of the left.

questions.solution_text:
The power is negative, so move the decimal point $3$ places to the left.
$6.4 \times 10^{-3}$
$=0.0064$

questions.question_text: A virus particle is $0.000\,000\,095$ m wide. What is this width written in scientific notation?

options.why: Counted the seven zeros instead of the eight places the decimal point moves.
Moved the decimal point one place too far, going past the first non-zero digit.
Used a positive power, but this width is a very small number so the power must be negative.

questions.solution_text:
The decimal point moves $8$ places to sit after the $9$.
$0.000\,000\,095$
$=9.5 \times 10^{-8}$ m

questions.question_text: Light travels about $9.46 \times 10^{12}$ km in one year. Write this distance as a basic numeral.

options.why: Moved the decimal point only eleven places instead of twelve.
Appended twelve zeros after $946$ instead of moving the decimal point twelve places from after the $9$.
Treated the power as negative and made the number small instead of large.

questions.solution_text:
The power $12$ is positive, so move the decimal point $12$ places to the right.
$9.46 \times 10^{12}$
$=9\,460\,000\,000\,000$ km

questions.question_text: Find the value of $n$ given that $3.9 \times 10^{n} = 0.000\,39$.

options.why: Counted the places correctly but kept the sign positive — a number less than $1$ needs a negative power.
Counted only the zeros after the decimal point instead of the places the decimal point moves.
Counted one place past the first non-zero digit.

questions.solution_text:
The decimal point moves $4$ places, and $0.000\,39$ is a small number, so the power is negative.
$n=-4$

questions.question_text: What is one hundred thousand, $100\,000$, written in scientific notation?

options.why: Counted the six digits instead of the five places the decimal point moves.
Moved the decimal point one place too few, counting only four of the five zeros.
Equal in value, but the coefficient $10$ is not less than $10$, so this is not scientific notation.

questions.solution_text:
The decimal point moves $5$ places to sit after the $1$.
$100\,000$
$=1 \times 10^{5}$
